name: cytotoxic-killing
title: Increment 7: NK/CD8 chemotax up the chemokine field and localize robustly (5/5 seeds); contact-killing WORKS in a close-contact test (1->0) — but at the DEFAULT full-scale scenario NK/CD8 never reach the infected cell, so end-to-end cytotoxic CLEARANCE is WEAK — capability proven, clearance an Increment-9 calibration gap

purpose.question:
Introducing NK (`types.K`) and CD8+ T (`types.E`) cells, wired to
chemotax up the macrophage-released chemokine field (Increment 6) and to
contact-kill infected cells via the CC3D source's literal LOCAL
(surface-contact) kill-rate formula: do NK/CD8 genuinely LOCALIZE toward
the infection (robust across seeds), does the contact-killing MECHANISM
itself actually clear an infected cell once contact happens, and — the
honest question this study exists to surface — does that killing
mechanism actually engage end-to-end at the scenario's own DEFAULT
full scale, or do NK/CD8 simply never get close enough within a
feasible step budget?

report.title: Increment 7: NK/CD8 localization is robust (NK mean change -20.37 vs control -1.02; CD8 -35.99 vs -0.54, 5/5 seeds) and contact-killing works in a close-contact test (infected 1->0 at ~update 22) — but at DEFAULT full scale NK/CD8 never reach the infected cell within budget (n_infected unchanged), so end-to-end clearance is WEAK — capability proven, clearance PENDING Increment 9
report.objective: Drive `run.run_cytotoxic_response` (Task 7.1 localization + Task 7.2 contact-killing, commit `4f28eba`) — the Task-7.1 three-cluster non-confluent scenario (`immune.build_cytotoxic_scenario_spec`: epithelial/infection patch | macrophage cluster | NK+CD8 cluster, every cluster INTERIOR, >= `margin_sites` from every noflux wall) over the Increment-6 macrophage/chemokine/IL-10 field stack, with NK/CD8 chemotaxis wired up the CHEMOKINE field (`immune. set_nk_cd8_chemotaxis`) and, each update, a contact-kill draw (`killing.contact_kill_rate`, the CC3D source's literal LOCAL surface-contact kill-rate form) for every still-infected cell against its NK/CD8 neighbor contact area. Measure (a) NK/CD8 mean distance-to-infection-centroid across 5 seeds (5, 17, 23, 42, 100), chemotaxis on (params.yaml's `nk.chemotaxis_v_nk`/`cd8.chemotaxis_v_cd8` x the documented `NK_CD8_CHEMOTAXIS_ENGINE_SCALE=100` engine-unit correction, Task 7.1) vs a lambda=0 control, 60 updates each; (b) a small, tight close-contact scenario (2 macrophages/2 NK/2 CD8, `margin_sites=4`, `separation_sites=1`, `steps=45`, seed=17) with killing enabled vs disabled, same seed; and (c) the DEFAULT full-scale scenario (6 macrophages/6 NK/6 CD8, `margin_sites=20`, `separation_sites=20`, `steps=60`, seed=17) with killing enabled, to check whether the killing mechanism actually engages at the scale this increment's own localization numbers were measured at.
report.conclusion: TWO SEPARATE, HONESTLY-DISTINGUISHED FINDINGS. (1) LOCALIZATION is robust: NK/CD8 mean distance to the infection centroid decreases in 5/5 tried seeds for both cell types (NK mean change -20.37, range -15.22 to -23.77; CD8 mean change -35.99, range -22.87 to -41.86), against a lambda=0 control with no consistent direction (NK mean -1.02, spread 7.59; CD8 mean -0.54, spread 4.52) — both mean gaps comfortably exceed their control's own seed-to-seed spread, and CD8 (2x NK's lambda) localizes more strongly than NK in every seed and on average, matching the paper's Sec. 2.3 "CD8+ sensitivity twice that of NK cells." (2) CONTACT-KILLING is a proven, working MECHANISM, not an end-to-end CLEARANCE result: a small close-contact scenario (2 macrophages/2 NK/2 CD8, `margin_sites=4`, `separation_sites=1`) kills the one infected cell (n_infected 1 -> 0 at update 22 of 45) with killing enabled, vs steady at 1 with the identical seed/scenario and killing disabled — proving `contact_kill_rate`'s contact-area lookup -> stochastic draw -> `types.D` transition engages correctly once NK/CD8 are in actual lattice contact with an infected cell. BUT at the scenario's own DEFAULT full scale (6 macrophages/6 NK/6 CD8, `margin_sites=20`, `separation_sites=20`, 60 updates, same seed=17 as the close-contact test), NK/CD8's mean distance to the infection closes substantially (NK ~81.6 -> ~57.8, CD8 ~81.6 -> ~39.8) but NEVER reaches actual contact within the run budget — `n_infected` stays at 1 for all 61 recorded steps, no kill fires. The killing CAPABILITY is proven; end-to-end cytotoxic CLEARANCE at default/realistic scale is NOT demonstrated here, and this study does NOT claim "NK/CD8 clear the infection" — only that the mechanism that would clear it, once contact happens, is implemented and verified correct.
report.main_insight: The weak end-to-end result is NOT a separate bug — it is the SAME root cause Task 7.1 already flagged for localization: the chemokine field's raw concentration in this engine's units is ~2-3 orders of magnitude smaller than the virus field's at comparable distances, so the source's literal chemotaxis lambda (5000/10000) is statistically undetectable against thermal/adhesion noise at this field's scale, requiring the documented, non-per-seed-tuned `NK_CD8_CHEMOTAXIS_ENGINE_SCALE=100` correction just to produce a MEASURABLE on/off localization gap — itself still far short of closing the FULL distance to actual contact within a feasible step budget. This compounds with `build_cytotoxic_scenario_spec`'s three-cluster layout (epithelial/infection patch -> macrophage cluster -> NK/CD8 cluster): NK/CD8 must close TWO cluster-separations' worth of distance to physically reach an infected cell, not one. Both are Increment-9 field-magnitude-calibration items, recorded not tuned away (per the brief's explicit instruction not to smuggle a rescue via re-tuning): if this study widened `NK_CD8_CHEMOTAXIS_ENGINE_SCALE` or shrank `separation_sites` until the default scenario also cleared the infection, that would hide the real finding (the source's literal parameters don't calibrate against this engine's field-concentration units) behind a number that looks better than the mechanism's honest state.
report.caveat: Kept fully visible, not resolved here: (1) 100x CHEMOTAXIS ENGINE-UNIT SCALE — `NK_CD8_CHEMOTAXIS_ENGINE_SCALE=100.0` (Task 7.1), a single, documented, non-per-seed-tuned correction; the literal source lambda values (5000/10000) are statistically undetectable at this engine's chemokine-field concentration scale. (2) DISCREPANCY #7 (resist-DIRECT) — `ContactKillingSteppable.step()` multiplies `kill_rate` by `cell_resist` DIRECTLY, not `(1 - cell_resist)`, unlike every other resistance consumer in this codebase; implemented literally per the source, not "fixed," flagged in `killing.py`, `run.py`, and `params.yaml`'s `nk.killing.kill_rate_resist_direct`/ `cd8.killing.kill_rate_resist_direct`. (3) NEARBY-POPULATION killing term deferred — `ContactKillingSteppable` also applies a well-mixed "nearby" (non-spatial) kill term (`params.yaml`'s `nk.killing.nearby_term_deferred`); only the LOCAL surface-contact term is modeled here, the nearby term requires Increment 8's population-scale ODE bookkeeping. (4) HAPTOTAXIS deferred — only field-gradient chemotaxis (toward the chemokine field) is modeled for NK/CD8 movement here; any adhesion/contact-gradient-driven (haptotactic) component of the source's fuller migration model is not implemented, an open Increment-9 item. (5) RECRUITMENT stubbed — a FIXED NK/CD8 population (6 cells each) is placed at scenario build time; chemokine-driven inflow/outflow (`params.yaml`'s `nk.recruitment`/`cd8.recruitment`) is not modeled. (6) 2D-APPROXIMATION geometry — the same non-confluent interior-placed 2D patch as Increments 5/6, not the source's z=2 immune-layer-over-confluent-z=1-sheet geometry. (7) CHEMOTAXIS FUNCTIONAL-FORM gap — the engine's fixed linear-lambda `World.set_chemotaxis` primitive, not the source's saturating, per-cell-COM-scaled `chemotaxis_v_nk / (1 + concentration)` form. (8) NO Figs 2/3A/3B/5/7 reproduction claim is made — verdict stays `documented`, NOT `passing`; the full reproduction verdict is PENDING until Increment 9 (the capstone).

study_card.goal: Validate that NK (type K) and CD8+ T (type E) cells, wired to chemotax up the macrophage-released chemokine field and to contact-kill infected cells via the CC3D source's literal LOCAL surface-contact kill-rate formula, actually (a) LOCALIZE toward the infection robustly across seeds, and (b) actually CLEAR an infected cell once genuine lattice contact happens -- while honestly reporting whether that killing mechanism engages at the scenario's own DEFAULT full scale, rather than only in an artificially close-contact test.
study_card.mechanism: The Task-7.1 three-cluster scenario (`immune.build_cytotoxic_scenario_spec`, every cluster interior-placed) extends the Increment-6 macrophage/chemokine/IL-10 field stack with NK+CD8 cells chemotaxing up the chemokine field (`immune.set_nk_cd8_chemotaxis`); each update, `killing.contact_kill_rate` (literal `ContactKillingSteppable` LOCAL form, resist-DIRECT per discrepancy #7) draws a stochastic kill for every currently-infected cell from its NK/CD8 contact-area neighbors (`world.cell_contact_area_by_type`), NK checked first, CD8 skipped if NK already killed that update (source ordering).
study_card.why_before_next: Increment 8 (global ODE coupling, APC-driven recruitment, the nearby-population killing term) and Increment 9 (the capstone reproduction) both assume the core NK/CD8 localization AND contact-killing mechanisms already work correctly in isolation before adding population-scale/ODE-coupled dynamics on top; this study establishes that both mechanisms are individually correct, while being explicit that they do not yet compose into end-to-end clearance at realistic scale -- a finding Increment 9's field-magnitude calibration needs to know about before it can be addressed, not hidden by tuning this study's own knobs.
study_card.expected_result: NK/CD8 mean distance to the infection centroid decreases substantially and consistently across seeds when chemotaxis is on, vs a near-isotropic lambda=0 control. A small, deliberately close-contact scenario shows the contact-kill mechanism actually removes an infected cell once NK/CD8 reach it. At the scenario's own default full scale, NK/CD8 close much of the distance but do not reach actual contact within a feasible step budget, so the infected count is unchanged -- reported honestly as a gap, not tuned away.
study_card.main_expert_question: The weak end-to-end result at default scale is the same chemokine-field-magnitude root cause Task 7.1 already flagged for localization alone (a single 100x engine-unit correction, not per-seed-tuned) -- should Increment 9's field-magnitude calibration treat chemotaxis lambda and contact-killing distance as one combined calibration target, or should the scenario geometry itself (cluster separation) also be recalibrated toward the source's true (non-2D-approximated) z=2 immune-layer placement, which may put NK/CD8 much closer to the infection than this study's 2D three-cluster layout does?

question:
Do NK (type K) and CD8+ T (type E) cells, chemotaxing up the macrophage-
released chemokine field and contact-killing infected cells via the CC3D
source's literal LOCAL surface-contact kill-rate formula, genuinely
LOCALIZE to the infection (robust across seeds) and genuinely CLEAR an
infected cell once contact happens -- and does that killing mechanism
actually engage end-to-end within a feasible step budget at the
scenario's own DEFAULT full scale, or only in an artificially
close-contact test?
hypothesis:
NK/CD8 cells placed in the domain interior, chemotaxing toward the
macrophage-released chemokine field via the engine's linear-lambda
`World.set_chemotaxis` primitive, will move up the gradient and
accumulate near the infection, robustly across seeds, with CD8 (2x NK's
literal lambda) localizing more strongly. Once NK/CD8 are in actual
lattice contact with an infected cell, `killing.contact_kill_rate`'s
stochastic draw will remove it (`types.I` -> `types.D`). At the
scenario's own default full scale, however, NK/CD8 may not close the full
distance to the infected cell within a feasible step budget -- if so,
that should be reported honestly as a weak end-to-end result, not
concealed by re-tuning the scenario/lambda until it "works."
objective:
Wire NK (`types.K`)/CD8+ (`types.E`) chemotaxis (`immune.
set_nk_cd8_chemotaxis`, Task 7.1) up the chemokine field (Increment 6)
and contact-killing (`killing.contact_kill_rate`, Task 7.2, the literal
`ContactKillingSteppable` LOCAL form) into the Task-7.1 three-cluster
scenario (`immune.build_cytotoxic_scenario_spec`) and driver (`run.
run_cytotoxic_response`), and measure: (a) NK/CD8 `mean_distance_to_
infection` across 5 seeds (5, 17, 23, 42, 100), chemotaxis on (lambda x
`NK_CD8_CHEMOTAXIS_ENGINE_SCALE=100`) vs a lambda=0 control (`tests/
test_influenza_nk_cd8.py::test_nk_and_cd8_localize_to_infection_across_seeds`,
task-7.1-report.md); (b) `n_infected` in a small close-contact scenario,
killing enabled vs disabled, same seed (`tests/test_influenza_killing.py::
test_infected_count_lower_with_nk_cd8_killing_than_without`,
task-7.2-report.md); (c) `n_infected` at the scenario's own DEFAULT full
scale with killing enabled, an ad hoc (not fast-pytest-suite) measurement
recorded honestly in task-7.2-report.md's "Honest assessment" section. A
minimal in-package figure (`pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/viz.py::
cytotoxic_killing_figure`, Task 7.3) renders the NK+CD8 distance
trajectory (on vs control overlay) plus the infected-count trajectory
(killing enabled vs disabled overlay).
description:
Increment 7 of the influenza-sego2022 capability ladder: introduces NK
(`types.K`) and CD8+ T (`types.E`) cell types, chemotaxing up the
Increment-6 chemokine field (NOT the virus field -- that stays the
macrophages' own chemotaxis target) and contact-killing infected cells via
the CC3D source's literal LOCAL surface-contact kill-rate term
(`ContactKillingSteppable`). Localization (Task 7.1) is validated across 5
seeds against an unbiased interior-placed lambda=0 control, following the
same fix-round-1 rigor Increment 5's macrophage-response study
established. Contact-killing (Task 7.2) is validated as a working
mechanism via a small, deliberately close-contact scenario -- and this
study's central honest contribution is reporting, rather than concealing,
that the SAME mechanism does not engage end-to-end at the scenario's own
default full scale within a feasible step budget: NK/CD8 localize but
don't reach actual contact, so no infected cell is cleared there. No
nearby-population killing term (Increment 8), no haptotaxis, no
chemokine/APC-driven recruitment dynamics (a fixed population is placed
at scenario build time), and no Figs 2/3A/3B/5/7 reproduction claim --
those are recorded in the caveats above, not modeled here.
claim:
NK/CD8 chemotaxis up the (unchanged, Increment-6) chemokine field
produces genuine spatial LOCALIZATION, robust across 5 tried seeds (NK
mean distance change -20.37, CD8 -35.99, both negative in 5/5 seeds,
against a near-isotropic lambda=0 control, NK -1.02/CD8 -0.54) with CD8
(2x NK's lambda) localizing more strongly than NK in every seed and on
average -- matching the paper's Sec. 2.3 "CD8+ sensitivity twice that of
NK cells." Separately, the contact-killing MECHANISM itself
(`killing.contact_kill_rate`, the source's literal LOCAL surface-contact
form, resist-DIRECT per discrepancy #7) is proven correct: a small
close-contact scenario kills the one infected cell (1 -> 0 at update 22
of 45) with killing enabled vs steady at 1 with the identical seed and
killing disabled. THIS STUDY DOES NOT CLAIM "NK/CD8 CLEAR THE INFECTION"
AT REALISTIC SCALE -- at the scenario's own DEFAULT full scale (same
6-macrophage/6-NK/6-CD8, 60-update scenario the localization numbers
above come from), NK/CD8 close much of the distance to the infection
(NK ~81.6 -> ~57.8, CD8 ~81.6 -> ~39.8) but NEVER reach actual contact
within the run budget, so `n_infected` is unchanged (stays at 1 for all
61 recorded steps, no kill fires). The killing CAPABILITY is
demonstrated; end-to-end cytotoxic CLEARANCE at default/realistic scale
is an OPEN Increment-9 field-magnitude-calibration item, the same root
cause as the localization mechanism's own 100x engine-unit-scale
correction, deliberately NOT tuned away here.
expected_behavior: NK and CD8 cells' mean centre-of-mass distance to the infected-cell centroid decreases when chemotaxis is switched on, consistently across multiple seeds, with CD8 (2x NK's lambda) showing a larger effect.
The same starting configuration, with chemotaxis switched off (an interior-placed, geometrically unbiased lambda=0 control), shows a small change with no consistent sign across seeds.
A small, deliberately close-contact scenario shows the infected-cell count drop to zero with killing enabled, vs remaining unchanged with killing disabled, same seed.

At the scenario's own DEFAULT full scale, the infected-cell count is NOT expected to drop within a feasible step budget -- NK/CD8 do not close the full distance to the infected cell in this run's step count, a result to be reported honestly, not tuned away.

This is the study's central honest finding: the killing mechanism itself is correct (see close_contact_n_infected above), but does not engage end-to-end at realistic scale. findings.statement:
NK cells chemotaxing up the (Increment-6, unchanged) chemokine field
via the engine's linear-lambda `World.set_chemotaxis` primitive
genuinely and consistently localize to the infection, at the
documented `NK_CD8_CHEMOTAXIS_ENGINE_SCALE=100x` engine-unit
correction -- robust across every one of 5 tried seeds, comfortably
beyond the lambda=0 control's own noise floor.

evidence.from_test: CD8 localization -- distance to infection decreases in every tried seed

findings.statement:
CD8+ T cells localize even more strongly than NK cells in every seed
and on average (mean on/off gap 35.45 vs NK's 19.35), consistent with
CD8's 2x-larger literal chemotaxis lambda (10000 vs 5000) and matching
the paper's Sec. 2.3 qualitative claim ("CD8+ sensitivity twice that
of NK cells").

evidence.from_test: Contact-killing reduces infected count vs. killing-disabled control
evidence.observed: n_infected: 1 -> 0 at update 22 of 45 with killing enabled; steady at 1 (unchanged) with killing disabled, same seed=17 and scenario

findings.statement:
The contact-killing mechanism (`killing.contact_kill_rate`'s literal
LOCAL surface-contact form, applied via a per-update stochastic draw,
NK checked before CD8 per the source's ordering) is implemented and
verified CORRECT: once NK/CD8 cells are in actual lattice contact with
an infected cell, the kill draw engages and removes it. This confirms
the killing MECHANISM works, isolated from whether NK/CD8 can reach an
infected cell at any particular scenario scale (see F-04).

evidence.observed: n_infected constant at 1 for all 61 recorded steps at the DEFAULT full-scale scenario (6 macrophages/6 NK/6 CD8, margin_sites=20, separation_sites=20, steps=60, seed=17); NK mean distance to infection closes ~81.6 -> ~57.8, CD8 ~81.6 -> ~39.8 over the same run -- substantial closing, but contact is never reached

findings.statement:
This is the study's central honest finding, reported as a GAP, not
hidden as a clean pass (status: partial): the SAME contact-killing
mechanism verified correct in F-03 does NOT engage end-to-end at the
scenario's own default/realistic scale within a feasible step budget
-- NK/CD8 localize (closing much of the distance, per F-01/F-02) but
never reach actual lattice contact with the infected cell, so no kill
draw ever fires. This is the SAME root cause as F-01/F-02's own
`NK_CD8_CHEMOTAXIS_ENGINE_SCALE=100x` engine-unit correction (the
chemokine field's raw concentration is far below what the source's
literal chemotaxis lambda was calibrated for), compounded by the
three-cluster scenario's extra cluster-separation distance. NOT tuned
away here, per the brief's explicit instruction -- an open
Increment-9 field-magnitude-calibration item.

conclusion:
LOCALIZATION MECHANISM VALIDATED (robust, 5/5 seeds, both NK and CD8,
CD8 stronger per its 2x lambda); CONTACT-KILLING MECHANISM VALIDATED as a
working, correctly-implemented primitive (close-contact test, 1 -> 0);
END-TO-END CYTOTOXIC CLEARANCE AT DEFAULT/REALISTIC SCALE IS WEAK -- NOT
DEMONSTRATED. NK/CD8 chemotaxing up the (Increment-6, unchanged) chemokine
field genuinely localize to the infection, robustly across 5 seeds for
both cell types, with CD8 localizing more strongly than NK (matching the
paper's stated 2x sensitivity ratio). Separately, `killing.
contact_kill_rate` (the CC3D source's literal LOCAL surface-contact
kill-rate form, resist-DIRECT per discrepancy #7) is implemented and
proven correct: a small close-contact scenario shows it removes an
infected cell once NK/CD8 reach it. But at the SAME scenario's own default
full scale (6 macrophages/6 NK/6 CD8, 60 updates, same seed as the
close-contact test) NK/CD8 never reach actual contact within the run
budget -- the infected count is unchanged. This study does NOT claim
"NK/CD8 clear the infection": the killing CAPABILITY is demonstrated, but
end-to-end clearance at realistic scale is an OPEN Increment-9
field-magnitude-calibration item, the same root cause as the localization
mechanism's own 100x engine-unit-scale correction, deliberately reported
as a gap rather than tuned away. Other open items, all recorded not
resolved: discrepancy #7 (resist-DIRECT kill rate), the deferred
nearby-population killing term (Increment 8), haptotaxis (not modeled),
stubbed recruitment (a fixed population), 2D-approximation geometry, and
the engine's linear (not the source's saturating/COM-scaled) chemotaxis
form. No Figs 2/3A/3B/5/7 reproduction claim is made -- that verdict stays
PENDING until Increment 9 (the capstone).

biological_summary:
NK (`types.K`) and CD8+ T (`types.E`) cells are placed in the domain
interior (the Task-7.1 three-cluster scenario: epithelial/infection patch
| macrophage cluster | NK+CD8 cluster, every cluster >= `margin_sites`
from every noflux wall) and wired to chemotax up the macrophage-released
chemokine field (Increment 6, unchanged) via the engine's linear-lambda
`World.set_chemotaxis` primitive, at the documented, non-per-seed-tuned
`NK_CD8_CHEMOTAXIS_ENGINE_SCALE=100x` correction (Task 7.1 -- the literal
source lambda is statistically undetectable at this engine's
chemokine-field concentration scale). Over a 60-update run, tested across
5 seeds (5, 17, 23, 42, 100), both NK and CD8's mean distance to the
infection centroid falls consistently when chemotaxis is on (NK mean
change -20.37, CD8 -35.99, negative in 5/5 seeds each), against a
near-isotropic lambda=0 control (NK -1.02, CD8 -0.54, no consistent sign)
-- CD8 (2x NK's literal lambda) localizes more strongly than NK in every
seed, matching the paper's Sec. 2.3 stated 2x-sensitivity ratio. Each
update, `killing.contact_kill_rate` (the CC3D source's literal LOCAL
surface-contact kill-rate form, applying `cell_resist` DIRECTLY per
discrepancy #7, NK checked before CD8 per the source's ordering) draws a
stochastic kill for every currently-infected cell from its NK/CD8 contact
area; a small, deliberately close-contact scenario (2 macrophages/2 NK/2
CD8, tight margin/separation) confirms this mechanism actually clears the
infected cell (1 -> 0 at update 22 of 45) once genuine lattice contact
happens, vs steady at 1 with killing disabled, same seed. This study's
central, deliberately UN-hidden finding: at the SAME scenario's own
DEFAULT full scale (6 macrophages/6 NK/6 CD8, the scale the localization
numbers above are measured at), NK/CD8 close much of the distance to the
infection (NK ~81.6 -> ~57.8, CD8 ~81.6 -> ~39.8 over 60 updates) but
NEVER reach actual contact within the run budget -- n_infected stays
unchanged at 1 for all 61 recorded steps, no kill fires. The killing
CAPABILITY is demonstrated and verified correct; end-to-end cytotoxic
CLEARANCE at default/realistic scale is NOT -- this is the same root
cause as the localization mechanism's own 100x engine-unit-scale
correction (the chemokine field's raw concentration is far below what the
source's literal parameters were calibrated for), compounded by the
three-cluster scenario's extra cluster-separation distance, and is
recorded as an open Increment-9 field-magnitude-calibration item rather
than tuned away. Discrepancy #7 (resist-DIRECT), the deferred
nearby-population killing term, haptotaxis, stubbed recruitment, and
2D-approximation geometry are all additional open items, not resolved
here.
key_assumptions: 100x CHEMOTAXIS ENGINE-UNIT SCALE — `NK_CD8_CHEMOTAXIS_ENGINE_SCALE=100.0` (Task 7.1), applied identically to NK and CD8's literal params.yaml lambda (preserving CD8's exact 2:1 ratio over NK), chosen from a one-time grid scan (50/200/500x) at a single seed then CONFIRMED (not re-tuned) across all 5 required seeds. The chemokine field's raw concentration is ~2-3 orders of magnitude smaller than the virus field's at comparable distances (chemokine diffuses ~87x faster, the same secreted mass spreads far more thinly), so the literal source lambda (5000/10000) is statistically undetectable against thermal/adhesion noise at this concentration scale -- a documented, non-per-seed-tuned engine-unit correction, an open Increment-9 calibration item.

DISCREPANCY #7 (resist-DIRECT) — `ContactKillingSteppable.step()` multiplies `kill_rate` by `cell_resist` DIRECTLY, not `(1 - cell_resist)`, unlike every other resistance consumer in this codebase (`transitions.infected_death_step`, `allee.*`, the secretion-scale gates). Implemented literally per the source, not "fixed" -- a cell with MORE local IFN is killed FASTER by contact NK/CD8, the opposite of every other resist-gated protective mechanism here. Left unresolved as recorded (possible intentional antigen-presentation effect, or a source inconsistency -- not adjudicated).

NEARBY-POPULATION killing term deferred — `ContactKillingSteppable` also applies a well-mixed, non-spatial "nearby" kill term (`params.yaml`'s `nk.killing.nearby_term_deferred`/ `cd8.killing.nearby_term_deferred`), independent of the LOCAL surface-contact term modeled here; requires Increment 8's population-scale ODE bookkeeping.

HAPTOTAXIS not modeled — only field-gradient chemotaxis (toward the chemokine field) drives NK/CD8 movement here; any adhesion/contact-gradient-driven directed-migration component is not implemented, an open Increment-9 item.

RECRUITMENT is stubbed — a FIXED NK/CD8 population (6 cells each) is placed at scenario build time; chemokine-driven inflow/outflow (`params.yaml`'s `nk.recruitment`/`cd8.recruitment`) is not modeled (requires the live immune-model ODE/SBML solver, Increment 8).

2D-APPROXIMATION geometry — the same non-confluent, interior-placed 2D three-cluster patch as Increments 5/6, not the source's z=2 immune-layer-over-confluent-z=1-sheet geometry. Faithful z=2 geometry is deferred to Increment 9, and may place NK/CD8 closer to the infection than this study's layout does (see report.main_expert_question).

CHEMOTAXIS FUNCTIONAL-FORM gap — the source uses a saturating, per-cell-COM-scaled lambda (`chemotaxis_v_nk / (1 + concentration)`); the engine primitive used here (`World.set_chemotaxis`) is a fixed LINEAR-regime lambda per (field, type). The fidelity criterion tested here is the localization/killing BEHAVIOR, not the exact functional form -- an Increment-9 calibration item.

END-TO-END CLEARANCE not demonstrated at default scale — reported honestly as this study's central gap (finding F-04), not tuned away by widening `NK_CD8_CHEMOTAXIS_ENGINE_SCALE` further or shrinking `separation_sites` until the default scenario also clears the infection; doing so would hide the real finding (the source's literal parameters don't calibrate against this engine's field-concentration units at any scale tried so far) behind a number that looks better than the mechanism's honest state.
No chemokine-driven APC/global-ODE-coupled recruitment amplification, no global ODE compartment, and no Figs 2/3A/3B/5/7 reproduction claim exist yet -- all later increments.

model_change.notes:
A new dashboard-loadable composite IS added this increment:
`pbg_cpm_studies.composites.influenza.cytotoxic_immunity` (Task 7.3) --
wraps the Task-7.1 three-cluster scenario + virus field (macrophage
chemotaxis, unchanged) + chemokine field (a NEW declarative spec entry,
`fields.chemokine_field_spec_entry`, Task 7.3), with NK/CD8 chemotaxis
wired declaratively via the chemokine field's `chemotaxis` list (the
same `cpm.schema.load_world` convention `macrophage_response` uses).
This is a LIVE-DEMO wrapper for the LOCALIZATION half ONLY -- it does
NOT implement the contact-killing step (`killing.contact_kill_rate` is
a custom per-update Python calculation over `world.
cell_contact_area_by_type`, not expressible in this declarative spec
format), and does not reproduce the field warmup or the
distance/n_infected readouts this study's measured numbers come from.
Those numbers (both the 5-seed localization table and the
close-contact/default-scale killing numbers) come directly from
`run.run_cytotoxic_response` (Tasks 7.1/7.2, a raw `cpm_core.World`
loop), not from this composite. `chemotaxis_v_nk=chemotaxis_v_cd8=0.0`
reproduces the localization lambda=0 control on the composite side too.
